description: Change of use of the ground floor premises from retail (Class E(a)) to a small restaurant/caf� (Class E(b)) with seating for approximately 25 customers.
decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - The applicant has failed to provide sufficiently clear, precise and unambiguous information and evidence to demonstrate, on the balance of probability, that the proposed use would be for the sale of food and drink principally to visiting members of the public where consumption would be mostly undertaken on the premises, so as to fall within Class E(b) of Schedule 2 to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended). In particular, insufficient information has been provided regarding the operational characteristics of the proposed business, including the anticipated balance and likely scale of on-premises dining compared with takeaway, customer collection and delivery activity. Whilst customer seating is proposed and the application describes the premises as a restaurant/caf�, the submitted plans and supporting information do not adequately demonstrate that the sale of food and drink for consumption on the premises would form the principal characteristic of the use. The Council is therefore unable to conclude, on the balance of probability, that the proposed use would necessarily fall within Class E(b) rather than amounting in substance to a sui generis hot-food takeaway. It has not been demonstrated that the proposed change from the established Class E(a) retail use would remain within Class E or would not constitute development requiring planning permission under Section 55 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
